name: Spondylocamptodactyly Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of congenital vertebral anomalies including scoliosis and vertebral fusion
Postnatal short stature with normal intelligence
Mild facial dysmorphic features such as broad nasal bridge and micrognathia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both major criteria (spinal malformations and camptodactyly) with supportive clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may assist but no specific gene mutation is definitively associated.

imaging: Radiographs showing vertebral segmentation defects and scoliosis
Hand X-rays demonstrating camptodactyly and phalangeal abnormalities
genetic: No definitive gene identified; possible autosomal dominant inheritance pattern suggested
other: Clinical assessment of joint contractures and growth parameters

distinguishingFeatures: More severe facial contractures and characteristic 'whistling face'
Presence of cleft palate and more pronounced craniofacial abnormalities
Multiple joint contractures present at birth involving large and small joints
Often associated with fetal akinesia and muscle hypoplasia

redFlags: Progressive respiratory insufficiency due to thoracic deformities
Rapidly worsening scoliosis in early childhood
references: Spranger J, et al. Spondylocamptodactyly syndrome: clinical and radiological features. Am J Med Genet. 1990.
